messages:
danielle_m: heads up — CS ticket C-5123. Multiple hosted customers hitting 503s from the inference API since ~10:12 UTC. Traces point to upstream inference worker exits/restarts on the gpu-pool-7 nodes.

danielle_m: snippet from customer request and error: 
```
POST /v1/generate (model=opt-13b-8bit, context=260k, batch_size=16)
...
E 10:12:34 runtime.cpp:456] RuntimeError: CUDARuntimeError: out of memory when allocating KV cache
E 10:12:34 worker.cpp:912] Received signal 11 (SIGSEGV), aborting.
container restarted (reason: CrashLoopBackOff)
```

kevin_sre: looking now — ops stream shows restart spike at 10:11:58 across three hosts in gpu-pool-7. Kube events show OOMKilled then CrashLoopBackOff.

ops-bot: alert: hosted-infer-prod/gpu-pool-7 restart_rate=4m (threshold=2m) — triggered 6 alerts.

maria_eng: can you grab `kubectl logs --previous` for one of the pods and the coredump backtrace? also need the model + quantization flags used by the runner.

danielle_m: pasted logs from pod infer-runner-7b2c: 
```
[2026-03-17T10:11:57Z] INFO prefetcher.cpp:120 Prefetching KV pages (size=2.1GiB) for request ctx_id=0x7f...
[2026-03-17T10:11:58Z] ERROR allocator.cpp:87 failed to allocate 536870912 bytes: CUDA out of memory (cur=14.3GiB, max=16GiB)
[2026-03-17T10:11:58Z] FATAL signal_handler.cpp:45 SIGSEGV at addr=0x7ffeeff0
#0 0x7f0a3 in kv_iterator::read() +0x2a
#1 0x6b1f4 in prefetch_worker::run() +0x114
#2 0x58dead in std::thread::_M_start_thread()
```

jen_support: customers impacted: acct-820 (prod traffic), acct-199 (low volume). CS already issued temporary retries and increased client-side backoff; need ETA for fix.

kevin_sre: quick mitigation ideas: 1) enable fallback routing to cpu/low-memory pool for these models, 2) reduce max batch_size for the route, 3) temporarily disable kv-prefetch on that model. I can flip a couple of those through the routing plane.

maria_eng: initial hypothesis — prefetcher is trying to page in KV cache for very large context sizes (>200k) and allocation accounting races with the runtime allocator. Repro steps I'm running locally with a dev runner:
```bash
# repro (dev):
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"opt-13b-8bit","input":"<very_long_context>","max_tokens":512,"batch_size":16}'
```
I can reproduce a CUDA OOM + segfault in the runner within ~2 requests.

danielle_m: flagged to infra — customers asking for ETA, CS wants clear workaround (pin model or reduce context).

kevin_sre: routing change applied: routed traffic for acct-820 and acct-199 to fallback pool (cpu-infer-1) at 10:23 UTC. Also scaled gpu-pool-7 by +2 nodes and set max_batch_size=8 for the affected route. Monitoring now.

ops-bot: change detected: route-updates/traffic-shift applied (id=ru-9982) — rollback window 30m.

maria_eng: dug into core: null pointer in prefetcher when page count calculation overflows 32-bit size_t for very large contexts. Patch ready: https://git.internal/redwood/infer/merge_requests/4321 — small fix plus defensive allocator check. Will run canary.

tom_lead: plan: canary deploy patch to one node in gpu-pool-7 (10:40 UTC), observe for 15m, then ship to pool if green. Also confirm hotfix doesn't change throughput drastically.

jen_support: told customers the workaround (pin to smaller context or reduce batch_size to 8) and that we're rolling a fix; they asked for status updates every 30 minutes.

kevin_sre: canary deployed at 10:40 to infer-runner-7b2c-canary. Early signs: no restarts for 5m, allocation patterns look stable.

maria_eng: confirmed fix address: bounds check and 64-bit arithmetic for page calc + immediate OOM guard. Added unit test + integration test that repros previous failure. PR approved; merging to release.

ops-bot: ci/pipeline passed for merge request 4321 — build 9876.

tom_lead: rolling patch to remaining nodes now with rate limit 1 node / 30s. Will keep route shift active until pool fully healthy (expected 11:05).

kevin_sre: health checks show restart_rate back below threshold on gpu-pool-7 at 10:59. Re-enabled normal routing for acct-199 at 11:05, acct-820 at 11:07 after smoke tests.

jen_support: CS notified customers at 11:12 UTC, ticket updated with root cause and mitigation. Customers accepted downtimes and were ok with the workaround while we rolled out fix.

maria_eng: postmortem notes to follow: root cause = integer overflow + missing allocator safety checks in KV prefetcher path on large-context requests -> OOM -> segfault -> container restart. Fix: MR 4321. Follow-ups: add context size quota at API layer, add runtime prefetch circuit breaker, and per-route max_context config.

danielle_m: closing loop with exec summary for C-5123 and handoff to postmortem; will include timeline and customer comms. Thanks all :thumbsup:

tom_lead: nice quick work. Marking incident resolved for now — will capture postmortem and action items. :white_check_mark:
